In Gaza, four Palestinians, including three children, were killed yesterday when a sand
cliff collapsed onto tents sheltering displaced families.
We have more from NPR's Anas Baba from Gaza City.
Huge boulders and tons of sand came crashing down from a steep bridge, onto a crowded tent
camp in Central Gaza.
The landslide buried several tents, neighbors frantically dug through the earth for survivors.
Those killed include one pregnant woman and three children, according to health officials.
The families had bitched their tents beneath the ridge, with little room to move elsewhere.
The Israeli military controls more than 70 percent of Gaza, leaving two million people
